title: Getting started with resquin
text: short tutorial describe functions resquin can use technical level. substantive introduction see (forthcoming) article Using resquin practice. Functions resquin calculate response quality indicators survey data stored data frame tibble. functions assume input data frame structured following way: data frame wide format, meaning row represents one respondent, column represents one variable. variables number response options. variables order questions respondents saw taking survey. responses integer values. Missing values set NA. (resp_styles()) Reverse keyed variables original form. items recoded.

title: Getting started with resquin
text: Consider following (fake) data set survey responses. data set contains responses three survey questions (var_a,var_b var_c) ten respondents. three survey question allow responses scale 1 5. respondents missing values, set NA. Lets use data set calculate response quality indicators.

title: Getting started with resquin
text: Response styles capture systematic shifts respondents response behavior. example, respondents extreme response style may choose lowest highest categories (example 1 5) mid-point responder choose midpoint scale (example 3). calculate response styles can use resp_styles() function. First, need specify data argument x. , need specify minimum maximum scales used questionnaire (scale_min scale_max respectively). Remember questions included must number response options. discuss arguments min_valid_responses normalize later. resulting data frame contains five columns corresponding middle response style (MRS), acquiescence response style (ARS), disaquiescence response style (DRS), extreme response style (ERS), non-extreme response style (NERS) - can learn response styles help file function using ?resp_styles. respondent receives one value indicator, given can calculated. normalize set TRUEthe values expressed share responses respondent can attributed response style. example, respondent one ERS value 0.67 meaning two three responses can identified extreme responses. hand, respondent one mid-point response, leading value 0 MRS column. Instead calculating proportions, can extract counts responses can attributed response option setting normalize FALSE. Finally, can decide include exclude respondents receiving response style values setting min_valid_responses, can take values 0 1. min_valid_responses sets share valid responses (.e. non-missing responses) respondent must receive response style values. value 0 indicates response style values calculated respondents, regardless whether missing values. value 1 indicates response styles calculated respondents valid responses variables. Values 0 1 indicate share responses need valid included response style calculations.
code: library(resquin) # Calculating response style indicators for all respondents with no missing values results_response_styles <- resp_styles(   x = testdata,   scale_min = 1,   scale_max = 5,   min_valid_responses = 1, # Excludes respondents with less than 100% valid responses   normalize = T)  # Presents results in percent of all responses  round(results_response_styles,2) #> # Number of missings due to min_valid_responses equal to 1: 4 #> # A data frame:                                             10 × 6 #>       id   MRS   ARS   DRS   ERS  NERS #>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #>  1     1  0     0     1     0.67  0.33 #>  2     2  0     0.67  0.33  0.33  0.67 #>  3     3  0.67  0     0.33  0     1    #>  4     4 NA    NA    NA    NA    NA    #>  5     5  0.67  0.33  0     0     1    #>  6     6  0     0.33  0.67  0.33  0.67 #>  7     7 NA    NA    NA    NA    NA    #>  8     8  0     0.33  0.67  0.67  0.33 #>  9     9 NA    NA    NA    NA    NA    #> 10    10 NA    NA    NA    NA    NA

title: Getting started with resquin
text: resp_distributions() calculates indicators reflect location variability responses within respondent. resp_distributions() works similar resp_styles(): need specify data argument can include exclude respondents calculations based amount missing data exhibit (explanation see paragraph ). resulting data frame contains eight columns: n_na: number intra-individual missing answers prop_na: proportion intra-individual missing responses ii_mean: intra-individual mean ii_median: intra-individual median ii_sd: intra-individual standard deviation mahal: Mahalanobis distance per respondent. can learn response distribution indicators using ?resp_distributions
code: # Calulating response distribution indicators for all respondents with no missing values results_resp_distributions <- resp_distributions(   x = testdata,   min_valid_responses = 1) # Excludes respondents with less than 100% valid responses  round(results_resp_distributions,2) #> # Number of missings due to min_valid_responses equal to 1: 4 #> # A data frame:                                             10 × 7 #>       id  n_na prop_na ii_mean ii_sd ii_median mahal #>    <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl> #>  1     1     0    0       1.33  0.58         1  2.04 #>  2     2     0    0       3.67  1.53         4  1.6  #>  3     3     0    0       2.67  0.58         3  1.38 #>  4     4     1    0.33   NA    NA           NA NA    #>  5     5     0    0       3.33  0.58         3  0.97 #>  6     6     0    0       2.33  1.53         2  1.38 #>  7     7     1    0.33   NA    NA           NA NA    #>  8     8     0    0       2.67  2.08         2  1.88 #>  9     9     2    0.67   NA    NA           NA NA    #> 10    10     3    1      NA    NA           NA NA

title: Getting started with resquin
text: resp_nondifferentiation calculates indicators primarily measuring known straightlining. However, different indicators measure different aspects straightlining. Simple Nondifferentiation just measures whether respondents used response option questions, indicators Mean Root Pairs Method Scale Point Variation Method provide continuous values nondifferentiation, measuring varied choice response options respondent . resp_nondifferentiation() works just like resp_distributions() resp_styles(). resulting dataframe contains four columns containing indicators described (Kim et al. 2019): simple_nondifferentiation: Respondents assigned 1 0 depending whether responses value (1) (0). mean_root_pairs: Mean root absolute differences pairs multi-item scale matrix questions. ranges 0 (least straightlining) 1 (straightlining). max_identical_rating: Proportion commonly selected response option among responses multi-item scale matrix questions. ranges 0 (least straightlining) 1 (straightlining). scale_point_variation: measure becomes larger respondents use scales points multi-item scale matrix questions. can learn response nondifferentiation indicators using ?resp_nondifferentiation.
code: results_resp_nondifferentiation <- resp_nondifferentiation(   x = testdata,   min_valid_responses = 1) # Excludes respondents with less than 100% valid responses  round(results_resp_nondifferentiation,2) #> # Number of missings due to min_valid_responses equal to 1: 4 #> # A data frame:                                             10 × 5 #>       id simple_nondifferentiation mean_root_pairs max_identical_rating #>    <dbl>                     <dbl>           <dbl>                <dbl> #>  1     1                         0            1                    0.67 #>  2     2                         0            0.21                 0.33 #>  3     3                         0            1                    0.67 #>  4     4                        NA           NA                   NA    #>  5     5                         0            1                    0.67 #>  6     6                         0            0.21                 0.33 #>  7     7                        NA           NA                   NA    #>  8     8                         0            0                    0.33 #>  9     9                        NA           NA                   NA    #> 10    10                        NA           NA                   NA    #> # ℹ 1 more variable: scale_point_variation <dbl>

title: Getting started with resquin
text: Response patterns describe suspicious response patterns arising careless insufficient effort responding. Careless insufficient effort respondents might choose answer option repeatedly (.e. creating long string equal responses) use pattern, zig-zaging, complete survey. resp_patterns() provides three columns contain longstring analysis indicators respondent. three columns always returned. two optional columns () analysis repeating response patterns: defined_patterns arbitrary_patterns: obtain three longstring analysis columns simply call resp_patterns(): obtain counts defined response patterns per respondents use defined_patterns argument. can either supply single vector representing response pattern, list vectors representing multiple response patterns. Finally, can request detection arbitrary response patterns counts larger one pattern lengths longer one using arbitrary_patterns argument
code: results_resp_patterns <- resp_patterns(testdata) round(results_resp_patterns,2) #> # Number of missings due to min_valid_responses equal to 1: 4 #> # A data frame:                                             10 × 4 #>       id n_transitions mean_string_length longest_string_length #>    <dbl>         <dbl>              <dbl>                 <dbl> #>  1     1             2                  1                     1 #>  2     2             2                  1                     1 #>  3     3             2                  1                     1 #>  4     4            NA                 NA                    NA #>  5     5             2                  1                     1 #>  6     6             2                  1                     1 #>  7     7            NA                 NA                    NA #>  8     8             2                  1                     1 #>  9     9            NA                 NA                    NA #> 10    10            NA                 NA                    NA # Single defined pattern defined_patterns_single <- resp_patterns(   x = testdata,   defined_patterns = c(1,2,3) ) defined_patterns_single #> # Number of missings due to min_valid_responses equal to 1: 4 #> # A data frame:                                             10 × 5 #>       id n_transitions mean_string_length longest_string_length defined_patterns #>    <int>         <dbl>              <dbl>                 <int> <list>           #>  1     1             2                  1                     1 <int [1]>        #>  2     2             2                  1                     1 <int [1]>        #>  3     3             2                  1                     1 <int [1]>        #>  4     4            NA                 NA                    NA <NULL>           #>  5     5             2                  1                     1 <int [1]>        #>  6     6             2                  1                     1 <int [1]>        #>  7     7            NA                 NA                    NA <NULL>           #>  8     8             2                  1                     1 <int [1]>        #>  9     9            NA                 NA                    NA <NULL>           #> 10    10            NA                 NA                    NA <NULL>  # Multiple defined patterns defined_patterns_multiple <- resp_patterns(   x = testdata,   defined_patterns = list( # wrap multiple pattern vectors into a list     c(1,2,3),     c(2,3,4),     c(4,3,2),     c(3,2,1)   ) )  defined_patterns_multiple #> # Number of missings due to min_valid_responses equal to 1: 4 #> # A data frame:                                             10 × 5 #>       id n_transitions mean_string_length longest_string_length defined_patterns #>    <int>         <dbl>              <dbl>                 <int> <list>           #>  1     1             2                  1                     1 <int [4]>        #>  2     2             2                  1                     1 <int [4]>        #>  3     3             2                  1                     1 <int [4]>        #>  4     4            NA                 NA                    NA <NULL>           #>  5     5             2                  1                     1 <int [4]>        #>  6     6             2                  1                     1 <int [4]>        #>  7     7            NA                 NA                    NA <NULL>           #>  8     8             2                  1                     1 <int [4]>        #>  9     9            NA                 NA                    NA <NULL>           #> 10    10            NA                 NA                    NA <NULL>  # defined patterns are returned as a single list column. # One way to make the data accessible is by using tidyr::unnest_wider() # This way, each column represents the count of one defined pattern  defined_patterns_multiple |>    tidyr::unnest_wider(defined_patterns) #> # A tibble: 10 × 8 #>       id n_transitions mean_string_length longest_string_length `1_2_3` `2_3_4` #>    <int>         <dbl>              <dbl>                 <int>   <int>   <int> #>  1     1             2                  1                     1       0       0 #>  2     2             2                  1                     1       0       0 #>  3     3             2                  1                     1       0       0 #>  4     4            NA                 NA                    NA      NA      NA #>  5     5             2                  1                     1       0       0 #>  6     6             2                  1                     1       0       0 #>  7     7            NA                 NA                    NA      NA      NA #>  8     8             2                  1                     1       0       0 #>  9     9            NA                 NA                    NA      NA      NA #> 10    10            NA                 NA                    NA      NA      NA #> # title: Response Quality Indicators for Survey Research
text: resquin (response quality indicators) provides functions calculate survey data quality indicators help identifying low-quality responses (Bhaktha, Silber, Lechner 2024; Curran 2016; Vaerenbergh Thomas 2013). resp_styles(), resp_distributions() resp_nondifferentiation() provide response quality indicators geared towards multi-item scales matrix questions. multi-item scales matrix questions present survey respondents multiple questions response format, meaning number labeling response options. moment, resquin provides four functions: resp_styles() - Calculates response style indicators (e.g. extreme response style middle response style). resp_distributions() - Calculates response distribution indicators (e.g. intra-individual mean standard deviation set survey questions). resp_nondifferentiation() - Calculates response nondifferentiation indicators. Nondifferentiation indicators primarily measure straightlining. indicators differ straightlining operationalized. Currently development. resp_patterns() - Calculates response pattern indicators (e.g. long string analysis). Currently development. (function response times also planed may require package. Data wrangling response times complicated.) information use resquin see vignettes Getting started resquin resquin practice. resquin still active development. Please use github issues file questions bug reports send directly matthias.roth@gesis.org. happy receive feedback!
